reviewers.summary: The prior bypass is closed, but the round-five mapping overapplies the check: unrelated public findings can now be rejected when a Cape Town record is pinned.

findingList.message: The public mapping marks every finding as relying on Cape Town evidence, so unrelated findings cannot be assessed when the basis contains that record unless they have a matching Cape Town specialist flag. Apply the requirement only to findings that actually rely on the evidence.

evidence.codePathTraced: ToClaim marks every public submission as relying on Cape Town evidence. When the accepted basis contains a Cape Town record, ResolveCapeTownEvidence throws if that claim has no exact matching Cape Town specialist flag.
evidence.failureScenario: An authorized presenter submits an unrelated finding for a case whose basis includes the Cape Town record, without a Cape Town flag matching its relatedRequirementId. Assessment rejects the finding even though it does not rely on the Cape Town evidence.

reviewers.summary: The public mapping closes the prior caller-controlled bypass, but its unconditional reliance flag also causes unrelated submissions to fail when Cape Town evidence is pinned. The changed tests cover omitted and false request fields for a Cape Town requirement, but not an unrelated public claim.

findingList.message: Marking every public claim as relying on Cape Town evidence rejects unrelated findings whenever the accepted basis contains that evidence. Apply the required flag check only to findings that actually rely on it.

evidence.codePathTraced: ToClaim marks every public submission as relying on Cape Town evidence. When the accepted basis contains a Cape Town interest pin, ResolveCapeTownEvidence requires an exact matching cape_town flag for every such claim.
evidence.failureScenario: A presenter submits an unrelated finding with a different relatedRequirementId, while the accepted basis contains the Cape Town evidence and no matching cape_town flag. The claim is rejected with InvalidDataException even though it does not rely on that evidence.

reviewers.summary: The round-five change removes the caller-controlled reliance field and marks public submissions as relying on Cape Town evidence during mapping. I found no remaining security vulnerability in the reviewed delta.
